course_name_original: INSTALACIONES INDUSTRIALES Y EN EDIFICIOS II
prerequisites: INSTALACIONES INDUSTRIALES Y EN EDIFICIOS I (565003347)
Proficiency in software packages, including word processors and spreadsheets

learning_outcomes.text: Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them working in multidisciplinary teams
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess the learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering
Knowledge and capacity for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Knowledge and capacity for the calculation and design of Industrial and Building Installations.
Knowledge and capacity for the calculation and design of Industrial and Building Installations.

syllabus_topics: Fire Protection Installations (FPI). Design, calculation and application
Natural Gas, Liquefied Petroleum Gases (LPG), Propane and Butane. Design, calculation and application
Energy certification of existing buildings CE3x program
teaching_methods: Classes in computer lab for practical application of knowledge in design and calculation of real building installations, fostering active learning and technical skills development in a simulated professional environment.

assessment_methods.method: Individual Work on Air Conditioning (CLI) and/or Energy Certification (CE3x)
Individual Work on Fire Protection Installations (PCI) and/or Renewable Energies (ER)
Exam on Fire Protection Installations (PCI) and Renewable Energies (ER)
Exam on Energy Demand (DE), Air Conditioning (CLI), Fuel Installations (IC) and Energy Efficiency (EE)

assessment_rules: The course can be passed through progressive assessment, provided all thematic blocks and associated practicals are approved. To pass the course, it is necessary to obtain a minimum score of 5 out of 10 in all activities assessed during the course, including blocks and practicals, in both ordinary and extraordinary calls. Blocks and practicals passed in the ordinary call will remain valid for the extraordinary assessment. The overall course grade will be the higher of the grade obtained throughout the semester and the grade corresponding solely to the final assessment.
